title: 3D Reconstruction of Neurons in Vaa3D v 3
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
materials: Navigate to the folder containing the tera-fly files
Space Bar or \: Reset view (very useful!)
Scroll wheel : Zoom within your current resolution
G: Toggle a grid on and off
V: Change colormap of skeleton (5 modes)
Different shades for each type (helps differentiate segments).
Loop detection, segments involved a loop will flash
You can connect two nodes with virtual finger
Save often but if the software crashes and you did not recently save look for a set of files called “autosave.xxx” from within your downloaded Vaa3D folder on your desktop.

steps.title: Download and install Vaa3D
steps.instruction: Navigate to the Vaa3D download page, click the “Get Started” link, download the entire Vaa3D folder and place it on the desktop, then launch Vaa3D by double‑clicking the .exe file.

steps.title: Install Visual C++ runtime if needed
steps.instruction: If an error “MSVCR120.dll Is Missing From Your Computer” appears, download the Visual C++ Redistributable package (vcredist_64x.exe, 2013 version) and run it to install the required DLLs.

steps.title: Prepare image stack
steps.instruction: Ensure the image stack (≈200–700 serial 2‑D TIFF images) is white‑on‑black; if not, invert the stack using Fiji (ImageJ) before conversion.

steps.title: Convert stack to Terafly format
steps.instruction: In Vaa3D select Advanced > Big‑Image‑Data > TeraFlyConverter, set input type to “TIFF (series, 2D)” and browse to the stack folder, set output type to “Vaa3D raw (tiles, 3D)” and choose a destination folder, then run the conversion.

steps.title: Open data in Mozak
steps.instruction: Launch Vaa3D again, open the converted Terafly data in the Mozak interface.

steps.title: Adjust view and hotkeys
steps.instruction: Use left‑click + drag to rotate, mouse wheel to zoom, Ctrl + A to rotate around the x‑axis, G + mouse wheel to change grid size, Ctrl + M to record a movie, and ensure Z‑Lock (hotkey L) is ON. Hotkeys for tools: polyline (P), auto‑z‑select (no hold), virtual finger (right‑click + drag, extend with E), lasso (Shift + hotkey, e.g., Shift + D to delete), retype (R), loop detection (V), disconnected mode (N).

steps.title: Create soma node(s)
steps.instruction: Press 1 to set node type to soma, activate the polyline tool (P), scroll to the optimal z‑plane, place the first node at the soma centre with a right‑click, then place a second node at the soma edge (at least two nodes are required for the soma type). Exit polyline mode by unchecking the button or pressing P again.

steps.title: Trace dendrites
steps.instruction: Select virtual finger, hold hotkey E, hover over the soma node and right‑click‑drag over dendritic signal; rotate the view after each segment to capture correct z‑depth. For finer control, use the polyline tool, placing each node at the centre‑of‑mass (highest intensity) on images 3 and 4 of a 5‑plane stack. Dendrites are thicker than axon; apical dendrite is the thickest, longest, most complex branch, usually heading toward the pia.

steps.title: Trace axon
steps.instruction: Identify the axon early (often exiting the soma or a basal dendrite). Use virtual finger (E) for continuous segments and the Mozak grid (G) to work square‑by‑square. The initial axon segment is thicker; distal axon is thinner and may branch at obtuse angles. When a short axonal branch is suspected, ensure at least five nodes are placed before labeling it a bouton (axon bouton rule).

steps.title: Exclude non‑neuronal structures
steps.instruction: Do not trace dendritic spines (require ≥3 nodes to be considered a branch), axon boutons (require ≥5 nodes), blood vessels, non‑specific surface labeling, or neurites from other patched cells. Verify each segment connects back to the main skeleton; use disconnected mode (N) to highlight isolated branches (light blue when connected).

steps.title: Save reconstruction files
steps.instruction: Use the Save As button to name the project; three files are generated: .ano, .apo, and .swc. Mozak loads the .ano file; to resume later, load the .ano via the “Load SWC” button. If only a .swc file exists, open Vaa3D, go to Plug‑In > linker_file and point to the folder containing the single .swc file.

steps.title: Measure soma radius
steps.instruction: Measure the long and short axes of the soma (e.g., with ImageJ), add the two values and divide by 4 to obtain the radius.

steps.title: Edit SWC radius column
steps.instruction: Open the .swc file in a text editor, locate the first row (type 1) and replace the default radius value 1.000 with the measured soma radius. Optionally delete the second soma node (second row with type 1) if present.

steps.title: Run Sorting Plugin
steps.instruction: In Vaa3D choose Plug‑In > IVSCC > IVSCC_sort_swc > sort_swc, and when prompted enter the soma node ID as the root number.

steps.title: Run Bulk post‑processing
steps.instruction: Open Vaa3D > Plug‑In > IVSCC > AllenNeuron_postprocessing > part 1. The plugin chain is: sort > resample (length 10) > sort > pruning (length 2) > sort > internode pruning > sort > Z‑smooth (length 10, optional) > sort. Select the sorted .swc file, answer “yes” to smooth the file, keep the pruning distance at 5, and confirm. Perform smoothing only once per file; answer “no” if the file has already been smoothed.

steps.title: Finalize radii and branch cuts
steps.instruction: Manually assign or interpolate radii where needed and mark branch‑cut ends to give the reconstruction a standardized appearance.

steps.title: Check connectivity and fix loops
steps.instruction: Toggle disconnected mode (N) to view unconnected branches (original colour) versus connected (light blue). Use loop detection (V) to highlight loops; split nodes until only one highlighted area remains, or delete the looped segment and retrace. If hotkeys stop responding, right‑click a small trace, delete it, and Vaa3D will reset.

steps.title: Expand collapsed stack if needed
steps.instruction: If the stack collapsed while using the polyline tool, go to the right‑hand toolbar, select Vaa3D Control > Volume Cut, and expand the Z‑cut.

steps.title: Export final SWC file
steps.instruction: After all processing, save the final reconstruction; the resulting .swc file contains node ID, x‑y‑z coordinates, radius, type, and parent ID for every node.
